findings.title: GS010 pre-check margin omits CALL-level charges, so the inner call can receive less than safeTxGas and a submitter can burn a tightly-estimated signed transaction
findings.description: The documented guarantee (docs/safe_tx_gas.md:21 and :39, and the code comment at Safe.sol:194-196) is that once the GS010 check passes, the inner call receives at least `safeTxGas`, so the relayer/submitter cannot influence whether a refund-mode transaction succeeds. The check `gasleft() >= max(safeTxGas*64/63, safeTxGas+2500) + 500` only budgets 500 gas for "code until the execution" plus the EIP-150 1/64 retention. It does not budget the gas the EVM charges to the *caller* at the CALL/DELEGATECALL opcode itself (Executor.sol:33/40) before the 63/64 rule is applied: cold account access of `to` (2600, EIP-2929), value transfer (9000 when value>0), new-account creation (25000 when value>0 and `to` is empty), nor the calldata->memory copy of `data` performed at the `execute(...)` call site (Safe.sol:203, ~3 gas per 32-byte word). With g' = gas remaining after those charges, the callee gets min(safeTxGas, g' - g'/64). If the submitter sets the outer gas limit so that gasleft at line 197 is just the threshold T = safeTxGas*64/63 + 500 (for safeTxGas >= 157,500), the callee receives safeTxGas - D where D ~= (63/64)*(C_pre + C_extra - 500) - stipend: ~2.3K for a cold value-less CALL, ~8.8K for a cold CALL with value, ~33K for a cold CALL with value to an empty account, plus ~3 gas/word of `data`. Because a failed inner call with safeTxGas>0 does NOT revert the outer tx (Safe.sol:207 only reverts when safeTxGas==0 && gasPrice==0), the nonce is consumed (Safe.sol:168), `ExecutionFailure` is emitted (Safe.sol:223) and, in refund mode, the submitter is still paid (Safe.sol:220). The outer frame only needs the retained 1/64 (~safeTxGas/63) to cover handlePayment + the event, so the attack is feasible when safeTxGas >~ 63 * post-execution cost (~700K gas for a native refund to the warm tx.origin; ~2-3M with an ERC-20 gasToken; ~150K in no-refund mode where only the LOG2 must fit) AND the signers estimated safeTxGas within D of the real need.
findings.attack_path: 1) Owners sign a Safe tx with gasPrice>0 (refund mode), safeTxGas=S estimated tightly (e.g. S = exact need, as eth_estimateGas on the inner call yields), to a contract not otherwise warmed in the tx, optionally with value>0. 2) A relayer (or in no-refund mode, anyone holding the public signatures) submits execTransaction with a gasLimit chosen so that gasleft() at Safe.sol:197 is just >= S*64/63 + 500 (the GS010 threshold). 3) At Executor.sol:40 the EVM first charges 2600 (+9000 [+25000]) to the Safe's frame, then forwards min(S, 63/64 of the remainder) = S - D; the callee runs out of gas and reverts. 4) success=false; since S>0 the outer tx continues: nonce has been consumed, handlePayment pays the relayer (gasUsed + baseGas) * gasPrice from the Safe, ExecutionFailure is emitted. The signed transaction is burned and must be re-signed, contrary to the documented 'relayer cannot influence the outcome' property. Requires S large enough that the retained S/63 covers the refund+event, and an estimate within D of the true need.
findings.evidence: Safe.sol:197: `if (gasleft() < ((safeTxGas << 6) / 63).max(safeTxGas + 2500) + 500) revertWithError("GS010");`  Safe.sol:194-196 comment: "some to perform code until the execution (500). We also include the 1/64 in the check ... to counteract potential shortings because of EIP-150."  Safe.sol:203: `success = execute(to, value, data, operation, gasPrice == 0 ? (gasleft() - 2500) : safeTxGas);` (calldata `data` is copied to memory here, after the check).  Executor.sol:40: `success := call(txGas, to, value, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0)` -- EVM charges access/value/new-account cost to the caller before applying the 63/64 cap to txGas.  Safe.sol:207 `if (!success && safeTxGas == 0 && gasPrice == 0)` -- failure with safeTxGas>0 does not revert; nonce incremented at Safe.sol:168; refund at :220; event at :223.  docs/safe_tx_gas.md:21: "the Safe contract will use the gas specified by the safeTxGas ... This is important to prevent that the relayer can increase the amount of gas used"; :39: "safeTxGas behaves like a 'minimum' gas value that needs to be available when it is set to a value > 0". Existing test test/core/Safe.Execution.spec.ts:226-260 even notes (line 257 FIXME) that gas used around the boundary is 'slightly higher than the safeTxGas', but no test exercises the starvation boundary.
findings.recommendation: Make the pre-check account for the charges the CALL opcode levies on the caller: e.g. compute `required = max(safeTxGas*64/63, safeTxGas+2500) + 500 + 2600 + (operation == Call && value > 0 ? 34000 : 0) + 3 * ((data.length + 31) / 32)` (or move the gasleft() check to immediately before the CALL inside execute and compare against `safeTxGas*64/63 + extras`). Alternatively, in refund mode, treat an inner failure as a hard revert when the forwarded gas could not have reached safeTxGas. At minimum, document in docs/safe_tx_gas.md that signers must add a buffer of ~2.6K (no value) / ~9K (value) / ~34K (value to a fresh account) plus 3 gas per word of `data` on top of the callee's estimate, and add a boundary test that drives gasleft at line 197 to exactly the threshold with a cold `to` and asserts the callee observed >= safeTxGas.

findings.title: setup() native-token deployment payment silently becomes 0 when tx.gasprice == 0 (handlePayment caps gasPrice=1 by tx.gasprice)
findings.description: setup() reuses handlePayment with `gasUsed=payment, baseGas=0, gasPrice=1` and the comment at Safe.sol:130-131 asserts `amount = (payment + 0) * 1 = payment`. However, for `paymentToken == address(0)` handlePayment computes `payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice < tx.gasprice ? gasPrice : tx.gasprice)` (Safe.sol:252), i.e. `payment * min(1, tx.gasprice)`. Whenever the deployment transaction has `tx.gasprice == 0` (zero-fee / private chains, local dev nodes, chains or bundles that accept 0-priced txs), the multiplier is 0: no native token is sent, no revert occurs, and setup completes as if paid. The ERC-20 `paymentToken` path (Safe.sol:256) is not capped and behaves as documented, so the two paths are inconsistent. The Certora refund spec explicitly works around this (certora/specs/NativeTokenRefund.spec: `hook GASPRICE uint v { require v > 0; ... }` with the comment 'We need to make sure that the gas price is not zero'), confirming the zero-gas-price case is known for execTransaction but it is not documented for setup, where the stated invariant is `amount = payment`. In the common case (paymentReceiver == 0 -> tx.origin == the deployer/relayer) the deployer only short-changes itself; it only matters when `paymentReceiver` is a third party that is owed the native-token `payment` (e.g. a deployment fee/escrow collected via setup).
findings.attack_path: On a network where transactions with tx.gasprice == 0 are mined (or any environment where the deployer controls tx.gasprice and 0 is accepted), a user deploys a Safe via SafeProxyFactory with initializer `setup(..., paymentToken=0, payment=X, paymentReceiver=<third party>)`. handlePayment computes X * min(1, 0) = 0, sends 0 wei to the receiver (call succeeds), and setup completes with the Safe fully configured while the receiver never gets X. No revert, no event discrepancy (SafeSetup omits refund info). On ordinary EIP-1559 chains tx.gasprice >= baseFee > 0, so this is not reachable there.
findings.evidence: Safe.sol:129-133: `if (payment > 0) { ... handlePayment(payment, 0, 1, paymentToken, paymentReceiver); }` with comment `amount = (payment + 0) * 1 = payment`.  Safe.sol:250-254: `if (gasToken == address(0)) { payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice < tx.gasprice ? gasPrice : tx.gasprice); (bool refundSuccess, ) = receiver.call{value: payment}(""); if (!refundSuccess) revertWithError("GS011"); }`.  Safe.sol:256: token path `payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice);` (uncapped).  certora/specs/NativeTokenRefund.spec lines 11-19: GASPRICE hook requiring v > 0 'because ... it'll come up with counterexamples'. Tests in test/core/Safe.Setup.spec.ts:343-400 only run with hardhat's default non-zero gas price.
findings.recommendation: Either document that the native-token setup payment (and execTransaction native refunds) is multiplied by min(gasPrice, tx.gasprice) and is therefore 0 on zero-gas-price transactions, or, if code size allows, have setup() bypass the cap (e.g. an internal `payNative(receiver, amount)` used by both paths, with the tx.gasprice cap applied only in execTransaction). Add a test with `gasPrice: 0` (hardhat `initialBaseFeePerGas: 0`) documenting the chosen behaviour.

result.reviewed: Read end-to-end: contracts/Safe.sol (setup, execTransaction, handlePayment, checkSignatures family, getTransactionHash), contracts/base/Executor.sol, contracts/common/SecuredTokenTransfer.sol, contracts/external/SafeMath.sol, contracts/SafeL2.sol (onBeforeExecTransaction ordering), contracts/base/ModuleManager.sol lines 80-200 (setupModules / execTransactionFromModule gas forwarding), contracts/base/GuardManager.sol lines 1-80 (ITransactionGuard hooks), contracts/accessors/SimulateTxAccessor.sol (how safeTxGas estimates are produced), docs/safe_tx_gas.md, docs/error_codes.md (GS010/GS011/GS012/GS013), CHANGELOG.md entries on gasleft removal, transfer/send removal (reentrancy note), and the 1.3.0 'revert on failure if safeTxGas and gasPrice are 0' change, certora/specs/NativeTokenRefund.spec and the gas-related rules in certora/specs/Execute.spec, test/core/Safe.Execution.spec.ts (all cases incl. 'should be possible to manually increase gas', payment-in-event tests, refund-receiver gas-forwarding test), test/core/Safe.Setup.spec.ts payment tests (lines 319-480), test/guards/ReentrancyTransactionGuard.spec.ts (nested execTransaction reentrancy), contracts/test/ERC20Token.sol, and the #1123 diff (git show f8fc2f2) for context. Hardhat/node_modules are not installed, so no tests were executed; all arithmetic (EIP-150 63/64, EIP-2929 access costs, value-transfer/new-account costs, LOG2 cost) was derived by hand from the Solidity 0.7.6 legacy-codegen semantics (left-to-right argument evaluation, calldata->memory copy at the execute() call site).
result.ruled_out: 1) `gasleft() - 2500` underflow (Safe.sol:203, unchecked in 0.7.6): GS010 guarantees gasleft >= 3000 at line 197; between the check and this gasleft() only ~200 gas of code plus the calldata->memory copy of `data` are spent, so underflow needs a submitter-chosen threshold gas limit plus >~500 gas of copy (>~5 KB data). If it does underflow the result is a huge txGas which EIP-150 caps to 63/64 of remaining -- behaviourally identical to 'all gas', and in that regime the outer tx is going to OOG/revert anyway. No exploitable state results. 2) `(safeTxGas << 6)` and `safeTxGas + 2500` wrap-around with huge signed safeTxGas: shown that no uint256 value makes both terms of the max() small simultaneously (small `S+2500 mod 2^256` requires S > 2^256-2500, then (S<<6)/63 ~= 2^250; small `(S<<6) mod 2^256` requires S ~= k*2^250, then S+2500 is huge), so GS010 always reverts for absurd values; 0.8.x panics instead -- same outcome, and the value is owner-signed anyway. 3) gasUsed computation: `gasUsed = gasleft(); ...; gasUsed = gasUsed.sub(gasleft())` -- gas is monotone decreasing so sub never reverts; `gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice)` overflows only with owner-signed absurd values and then reverts the whole tx (nonce not consumed) via SafeMath's bare require. gasUsed correctly includes the calldata copy and CALL-level charges that the Safe actually paid, so the refund cannot exceed (safeTxGas + ~37K extras + baseGas) * gasPrice, all bounded by signed parameters. 4) Relayer profit via gas inflation in refund mode: callee gas is capped at safeTxGas (Safe.sol:203/Executor.sol:40); CALL extras are bounded (cold 2600 / value 9000 / new account 25000) and the relayer can only reduce them (access lists), not increase them; token path has no tx.gasprice cap by design (token price incomparable) but gasPrice/gasToken/baseGas are all in the signed hash (Safe.sol:530-534). 5) Reentrancy during refund (Safe.sol:253 full-gas call; Safe.sol:257 transferToken with gas-10000; ERC-777/hook gasTokens; EIP-7702 tx.origin): at that point nonce is already incremented (Safe.sol:168) and signatures consumed; a re-entrant execTransaction needs valid signatures for the next nonce, module paths need module privilege, and no Safe storage is written after the refund (only events and the guard's checkAfterExecution). The only observable effect is nested event/guard-hook ordering (inner ExecutionSuccess before outer), which is exactly the nesting already reachable via `to == address(this)` and covered by test/guards/ReentrancyTransactionGuard.spec.ts; guards that care can block it as the example guard does. Not a finding. 6) transferToken return-data handling (SecuredTokenTransfer.sol:27-37): output written to scratch space [0,0x20) which is legitimate for memory-safe assembly; returndatasize 0 -> success flag (USDT-style), 0x20 -> success && word != 0, anything else -> false -> GS012 revert (whole tx reverts, nonce not consumed). A code-less gasToken yields success with 0 returndata and the payment is silently skipped -- documented in the NatSpec ('doesn't check if the token address is a contract') and only harms the relayer/deployer who chose/accepted it. `sub(gas(), 10000)` wraps in assembly if gas < 10000 but EIP-150 then just forwards 63/64; harmless. 7) Revert bubbling (Safe.sol:207-216): copies the inner call's returndata to the free memory pointer and reverts; no external call intervenes between Executor's CALL and this block, so returndata is the callee's; the nonce++ is rolled back too, matching docs/safe_tx_gas.md:49-66; huge returndata only causes OOG which is still a revert. 8) `safeTxGas == 0 && gasPrice > 0` gives the inner call 0 gas (plus 2300 stipend if value>0), so it only succeeds for EOA/value-transfer targets -- documented 1.3.0 behaviour (CHANGELOG 'Revert on failure if safeTxGas and gasPrice are 0', docs/safe_tx_gas.md) and exercised by test/core/Safe.Execution.spec.ts:113-123 and :312-349. 9) Executor DELEGATECALL ignores `value` (Executor.sol:33): EVM has no value for DELEGATECALL; the signed `value` is still hashed (Safe.sol:527) and shown to the guard (Safe.sol:178) but has no effect -- misleading UX at most, no attack path since a delegatecall target already has full Safe authority; informational, not reported. 10) 2500-gas reserve for events: ExecutionSuccess/Failure are LOG2 with 32 bytes data (~1.4K), fits; in refund mode handlePayment's own CALL (>= 9.1K to warm tx.origin) is not covered by the reserve, but running out there reverts the whole tx (nonce restored) and only costs the relayer. 11) execTransaction is payable: msg.value simply accrues to the Safe; no accounting interaction with the refund. 12) tx.origin refund receiver: a reverting receiver (contract or 7702-delegated EOA) triggers GS011 and a full revert, self-inflicted by the submitter; ERC-4337 flows do not use execTransaction refunds. 13) `gasPrice < tx.gasprice ? gasPrice : tx.gasprice` under EIP-1559: tx.gasprice is the effective price, so the cap is correct; a zero tx.gasprice zeroes the native refund in execTransaction, which the Certora spec already treats as a known precondition (only the setup() variant with its explicit 'amount = payment' claim is reported above, as informational). 14) #1115 (SecuredSignatureValidator) and #1123 (simulate revert length) have no gas/refund interaction: checkSignatures runs before the GS010 gasleft() snapshot, so any extra gas they consume is simply paid by the submitter and never affects the inner-call budget or the refund.

findings.title: docs/signatures.md does not document the v == 2 secp256r1 signature encoding
findings.description: The signature-format specification enumerates only ECDSA (26 < v < 31), eth_sign (v > 30), contract (v == 0) and pre-validated (v == 1) types. The implementation in contracts/Safe.sol:354-396 also accepts v == 2 (RIP-7212/EIP-7951 secp256r1), whose constant part is `{32-byte owner}{32-byte data pointer}{0x02}` and whose dynamic part is a fixed 128-byte `{r}{s}{qx}{qy}` block *without* a length prefix (unlike the contract-signature dynamic part), and whose owner address is defined as `keccak256(qx || qy)[12:]`. None of this is in the spec; the only description is a code comment and the tests. Integrators that parse/validate `signatures` bytes from the spec (guards, relayers, indexers, nested-Safe tooling) will treat v == 2 as an invalid/ECDSA type and mis-split the dynamic region.
findings.attack_path: No direct exploit. Correctness/robustness gap: an off-chain or guard-side parser written against docs/signatures.md will misinterpret the 128-byte secp256r1 dynamic part (e.g. read it as a length-prefixed contract signature) and could reject valid transactions or mis-attribute signers.
findings.evidence: docs/signatures.md:13-69 lists only four types. contracts/Safe.sol:354-368: `} else if (v == 2) { ... if (uint256(s) < requiredSignatures.mul(65)) revertWithError("GS021"); if (uint256(s).add(128) > signatures.length) revertWithError("GS027");` and :393 `signerAddress := keccak256(add(sig, 0x40), 0x40)`. docs/error_codes.md:50-55 mentions GS027/GS028 but not the byte layout.
findings.recommendation: Add a `secp256r1 signature (signature type == 2)` section to docs/signatures.md describing the constant part, the 128-byte unprefixed dynamic part, the owner-address derivation `keccak256(qx||qy)[12:]`, and the accepted malleability (no low-s enforcement), mirroring the code comment at Safe.sol:355-360.

findings.title: Contract-signature offset near 2^256 reverts with a SafeMath string instead of a GS error code
findings.description: `checkContractSignature` bounds-checks the data pointer with `offset.add(32)` (SafeMath). For an attacker-supplied pointer `s >= 2^256 - 32`, SafeMath reverts with the string `"SafeMath: addition overflow"` rather than `GS022`. The same applies to `offset.add(32).add(contractSignatureLen)` at line 282 and `uint256(s).add(128)` at line 368 (GS027). PR #1115 explicitly set the goal of 'consistent use of error codes across the signature validation logic' and of not letting the `signatures` bytes steer the revert data; this path still yields a non-GS revert reason driven by the signature bytes (the string is constant, so it is not attacker-controlled data, only an inconsistency). Confirmed empirically: a v=0 signature with s = 0xff..ff reverts, but not with GS022.
findings.attack_path: None. The revert is total and the string is constant; the only effect is that tooling matching on `GS0xx` codes sees an unexpected reason.
findings.evidence: contracts/Safe.sol:272 `if (offset.add(32) > signatures.length) revertWithError("GS022");` ; :282 `if (offset.add(32).add(contractSignatureLen) > signatures.length) revertWithError("GS023");` ; :368 `if (uint256(s).add(128) > signatures.length) revertWithError("GS027");`. PoC (hardhat, 0.7.6): signature `owner || 0xff*32 || 0x00` on a 1-of-1 Safe reverts without the GS022 reason.
findings.recommendation: Use overflow-free comparisons, e.g. `if (offset > signatures.length || signatures.length - offset < 32) revertWithError("GS022");` and analogously for GS023/GS027, so every malformed-signature path reverts with a GS code.

Ran the existing test/core/Safe.Signatures.spec.ts (65 passing, 0.7.6 build) and the @secp256r1 subset with HARDHAT_SECP256R1_PRECOMPILE=1 (4 passing). Wrote and ran a temporary PoC spec (kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-safe-smart-account/df1930e0-11e2-50b6-a436-b966e6fde9f0/scratchpad/Zz.AuditPoc.spec.ts, removed from the repo) covering: v=1 r=0 with executor=0; v=1 r=SENTINEL with executor=SENTINEL; v in {3,4,26,29,30,33..38,255} with a genuine owner r,s; contract signature for EOA owner and for the identity precompile 0x04; isValidSignature returning 32 clean / 36 bytes / 32 dirty-low-bytes / 4 bytes; contract-signature pointer aliasing an extra unprocessed static part; pointer near 2^256; secp256r1 with an EOA owner as r, and with malleated s (n - s) under the precompile. All 8 cases behaved as reasoned (no bypass).
result.ruled_out:
1. Out-of-bounds reads in the packed buffer: GS020 (Safe.sol:319) guarantees [0, requiredSignatures*65) is in bounds; signatureSplit reads r/s fully inside and v via byte(0, mload(pos*65+64)) whose only used byte is in bounds (over-read of up to 31 bytes of memory beyond the buffer is harmless). v=0: GS021 (:341) + GS022 (:272) + GS023 (:282) with SafeMath make [offset, offset+32+len) in bounds before mload/abi.encode. v=2: GS021 (:367) + GS027 (:368) make [s, s+128) in bounds. No OOB.
2. Aliasing of the dynamic pointer with static parts when more than `requiredSignatures` signatures are supplied (documented at :339-340): the pointer may land in an *unprocessed* extra static part (confirmed by PoC), but it can never overlap the processed static region [0, N*65), and the data at the pointer is attacker-chosen bytes in any case; each owner validates its own bytes independently, so no forgery or threshold reduction is possible. Pointers of two contract signatures may coincide — legitimate.
3. ecrecover returning address(0): caught by `currentOwner <= lastOwner` with lastOwner initialised to 0 (:321, :405) and by `owners[0] == 0` (OwnerManager never stores a mapping entry for address(0)). v in 3..26, 29, 30 go to the plain ecrecover branch and return 0; v >= 33 goes to the eth_sign branch with v-4 not in {27,28} and returns 0; v=31/32 are the only eth_sign values. No underflow in `v - 4` since v > 30. All confirmed by PoC (GS026).
4. Duplicate owner with mixed signature types (contract sig for X + ECDSA for X, approved-hash for X + ECDSA for X): the strict ascending check at :405 compares the *resolved* owner regardless of type; covered by existing tests and by construction. secp256r1 + ECDSA for the same address is impossible (would need a keccak preimage of qx||qy ending in an EOA address).
5. v=1 with executor spoofing: in execTransaction the executor is the real msg.sender of the Safe (:170); HandlerContext._msgSender() only affects handlers (which pass address(0) as executor: CompatibilityFallbackHandler.sol:83, SignatureVerifierMuxer.sol:159). v=1 with r=0 and executor=0 passes the GS025 check but fails `currentOwner <= lastOwner`; r=SENTINEL fails the explicit `currentOwner == SENTINEL_OWNERS` check (needed because owners[0x1] is non-zero). Both confirmed by PoC. Self-call auto-approval (msg.sender == address(this)) only matters for EIP-7702 accounts that list themselves as owner (OwnerManager.sol:120 blocks it otherwise); every path that makes such a Safe call itself is already authorised (module, signed Safe tx) or fully reverted (simulateAndRevert at StorageAccessible.sol:39-45, CompatibilityFallbackHandler.simulate).
6. secp256r1 path: owner address = keccak256(qx||qy)[12:]; using an EOA/contract owner's address as r requires a keccak preimage — infeasible (PoC: GS028). `signerAddress` is assigned from assembly with dirty high bits, but Solidity cleans both operands before `!=` (legacy codegen cleanupNeededForOp returns true for compare ops); confirmed by the passing @secp256r1 tests. Point validity (on-curve, non-infinity, r,s in range) is enforced by the precompile; EIP7951.sol:39-44 only accepts `success && returndatasize()==32 && word==1`, and a missing precompile yields returndatasize 0 → false → GS028. Input is exactly 160 bytes as EIP-7951 requires. s-malleability is documented/accepted (:359-360) and confirmed by PoC; nonce prevents replay.
7. Contract signatures / #1115: staticcall forwards 63/64 gas; an OOG in the callee makes the Safe revert with GS024, which is the same terminal outcome as the pre-change propagated revert (no path interprets GS024 as a non-reverting 'false'). Reentrancy is impossible (STATICCALL). Return-bomb griefing offers no amplification because the callee must itself expand memory to return N bytes. EOA/precompile/no-code 'owners' return empty or wrong-length data → GS024 (PoC: EOA owner and identity precompile 0x04 both GS024; previously 0x04 as an owner would have been a universal signer with the v1 ABI decoder, now rejected). `result.length == 32 && abi.decode(result,(bytes32)) == bytes32(EIP1271_MAGIC_VALUE)` requires exactly `0x1626ba7e` + 28 zero bytes, matching ABI encoding of bytes4 from Solidity and Vyper; 4-byte raw returns were already rejected by the 0.7.6 decoder (returndatasize < 32). Behaviour is identical on 0.7.6 and 0.8.x. The CHANGELOG documents the breaking strictness. The validator is called *before* the owner-membership check (GS026), but it is a staticcall with a fixed selector/dataHash, so making the Safe staticcall an arbitrary address has no state effect. Self-ownership (7702) recursion through CompatibilityFallbackHandler re-hashes into a SafeMessage at every level and is gas-bounded; it bottoms out in GS025/GS024 (existing test) and cannot reduce the threshold.
8. approvedHashes: approvals persist forever (documented ISafe.sol:147); tx hashes embed nonce+domain so no replay via execTransaction; message-hash approvals are intended to persist. `approveHash` membership check `owners[msg.sender] != 0` would pass for msg.sender == 0x1 (sentinel) but 0x1 cannot originate calls.
9. Nonce ordering: `nonce++` (:168) happens before checkSignatures and before the guard; a failed signature check reverts the increment. Guards observing nonce+1 is long-standing 1.3.0+ behaviour; the guard runs after signature validation and is trusted. SafeL2 emits the pre-increment nonce (SafeL2.sol:74).
10. getTransactionHash assembly (:503-547): calldataHash is computed before the struct overwrites ptr; 11 words = 352 bytes hashed; `mstore(ptr, 0x1901)` places 0x19 0x01 at ptr+30..31 and `keccak256(add(ptr,30), 66)` covers prefix||domainSeparator||structHash — matches the TS reference (test passes 100 random cases). `to`/`gasToken`/`refundReceiver`/`operation` are cleaned/validated on calldata load; `_nonce` is uint256. Memory-safety: writes beyond the free pointer are scratch only.
11. #1123: `revert(add(response, 0x20), mload(response))` is correct — response is laid out as [len][data] copied from returndata[0x20:], so exactly `len` bytes are re-thrown (previously len+32).
12. Chain/cross-Safe replay: domainSeparator is computed with the live `chainid()` and `address()` (:461-472); nested-Safe contract signatures are bound to the inner Safe's domain via SafeMessage.
13. 0.7.6 unchecked arithmetic: all signature-path arithmetic uses SafeMath or is bounded (`mul(0x41,pos)` with pos < N where N*65 <= length; `v - 4` with v > 30).
14. Legacy `checkSignatures(bytes32,bytes,bytes)` / `checkNSignatures(bytes32,bytes,bytes,uint256)` use msg.sender as executor and ignore `data` — explicitly documented with warnings (:416, :432); `checkNSignatures(...,0)` succeeding with no signatures is intended and tested.

findings.title: EIP-7702 delegation to the Safe singleton without an atomic `setup` leaves threshold == 0, so anyone can initialize and take over the account; acknowledged only in a test-helper comment, not in user-facing docs
findings.description: `setupOwners` relies solely on `if (threshold > 0) revertWithError("GS200")` (contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:49) to prevent re-initialization, and `Safe.setup` (contracts/Safe.sol:108-134) has no caller restriction. For proxies this is safe because `SafeProxyFactory.deployProxy` runs the initializer in the same transaction (contracts/proxies/SafeProxyFactory.sol:66-77). Version 1.5.0 adds first-class EIP-7702 support (contracts/common/EIP7702.sol; contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:120 allows the account to be its own owner when delegated; tests in test/core/Safe.OwnerManager.spec.ts:60-68, test/core/Safe.Setup.spec.ts:169-186). An EOA that delegates directly to the `Safe`/`SafeL2` singleton has all-zero storage, i.e. `threshold == 0`, so until the owner's own `setup` call lands, `setup` is callable by anyone. The repository acknowledges this only inside the test helper `getEip7702SafeTemplateWithSingleton` (test/utils/setup.ts:122-123: "this process is UNSAFE and only used for testing ... can be front-run by anyone"); nothing in docs/overview.md, docs/error_codes.md, CHANGELOG.md, or the `ISafe.setup`/`IOwnerManager` natspec warns integrators. A runnable PoC already exists in this checkout at docs/security-review/poc/eip7702-setup-frontrun.spec.ts (added by an earlier stage). This is an inherent property of any initializer pattern under EIP-7702 and not a defect in the manager code, hence informational.
findings.attack_path: 1) Victim EOA signs an EIP-7702 authorization for the Safe (or SafeL2) singleton. 2) The type-4 transaction that carries it (sent by the victim or by a relayer the victim handed the authorization to) does not call `setup` on the EOA in the same transaction. 3) Attacker observes the delegation and calls `victimEOA.setup([attacker], 1, 0, "", 0, 0, 0, 0)`; `setupOwners` passes because `threshold == 0` (OwnerManager.sol:49) and `setupModules` passes because `modules[SENTINEL] == 0` (ModuleManager.sol:89). 4) Attacker is now the sole owner and drains the EOA through `execTransaction`. The victim's later `setup` reverts with GS200.
findings.evidence: contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:46-53 (`if (threshold > 0) revertWithError("GS200")` is the only re-init guard); contracts/Safe.sol:108-127 (`setup` is `external` with no caller check); contracts/base/ModuleManager.sol:88-90; contracts/proxies/SafeProxyFactory.sol:66-77 (atomic initializer for the proxy path only); test/utils/setup.ts:121-133 (helper delegates to the singleton in one tx and calls `setup` in a later one, with an explicit UNSAFE comment); docs/security-review/poc/eip7702-setup-frontrun.spec.ts (existing PoC demonstrating takeover and drain).
findings.recommendation: Add a user-facing warning (docs/overview.md and the `ISafe.setup` natspec, ideally the CHANGELOG entry for EIP-7702 support) stating that an EIP-7702 delegation to the Safe singleton MUST be combined with the `setup` call in the same transaction (type-4 tx with `to = self`, `data = setup(...)`), or that integrators should delegate to a proxy that commits to the setup parameters (as done by the separate safe-eip7702 proxy). No contract change is required; optionally keep the existing PoC spec as a regression/documentation test.

result.ruled_out:
1) Owner linked-list corruption (OwnerManager.sol:76-143): addOwnerWithThreshold inserts at the head only after requireCanAddOwner (L128-132: not 0/sentinel/self-unless-7702 and owners[owner]==0); removeOwner/swapOwner require owners[prevOwner]==owner (L142) and, because the mapping holds non-zero values only for the sentinel and current members (entries are zeroed at L95/L109), prevOwner is forced to be a list member; self-loops (owners[x]==x) are never written; swapOwner with newOwner==oldOwner or newOwner==prevOwner fails GS204. ownerCount is only written at L69/L80/L92 and swap leaves it untouched, so it cannot desync. Threshold math: L92 pre-decrements and compares against the NEW _threshold, changeThreshold (L148-155) enforces 1<=t<=ownerCount, and skipping changeThreshold when _threshold==threshold (L83/L98) is safe because ownerCount only grew (add) or was just checked against the same value (remove). The unchecked `--ownerCount` at ownerCount==0 is unreachable on an initialized Safe (GS202/GS201 force >=1 owner) and on the singleton requireCanRemoveOwner fails anyway. Non-consecutive duplicate owners in setupOwners are caught by the mapping check (L131), consecutive ones by L63. All covered by the 73 passing tests.
2) Re-initialization via threshold==0: the only guard is L49, but threshold is set to 1 in the singleton constructor (Safe.sol:102), can never be set to 0 through changeThreshold (L152), and can only be zeroed by a raw storage write via DELEGATECALL (execTransaction delegatecall, module delegatecall, or the setup initializer at ModuleManager.sol:94) — all owner/module-trusted. Even then a second `setup` is blocked by GS100 (ModuleManager.sol:89) unless modules[SENTINEL] is zeroed too; the practical result would be a self-inflicted brick (GS001), not a takeover. The only realistic zero-threshold state is a fresh EIP-7702 delegation, reported above as informational.
3) `authorized` reachability (SelfAuthorized.sol:16): msg.sender==address(this) is reachable from execTransaction(to=self), execTransactionFromModule(to=self), any DELEGATECALL target making an external call to address(this) (this is how SafeMigration.sol:82/99 and setup initializers work), and from simulateAndRevert's delegatecall (always reverted, see 11). None grants capability the caller did not already have. Fallback handlers and guards are CALLed, so their callbacks arrive with msg.sender==handler/guard and fail GS031.
4) Safe as its own module: enableModule has no self check (ModuleManager.sol:144) and my PoC confirmed that after `enableModule(safe)` a signed `execTransaction(to=safe, data=execTransactionFromModule(target, 0, data, DelegateCall))` passes the module check (L117) while the transaction guard only sees a CALL to self. Not a new consequence: the same signers can enable any module (the guard sees `enableModule` in both cases) or batch enableModule+call through MultiSendCallOnly; modules are documented as fully trusted and outside the transaction guard. Informational at most, not reported.
5) Module list / pagination (ModuleManager.sol:142-162, 217-248): zero and sentinel rejected (L144/L157); the sentinel has a non-zero mapping value so GS104 explicitly excludes it (L117, tested in Safe.ReservedAddresses.spec). getModulesPaginated validates `start`, and `next = array[moduleCount-1]` correctly returns the last element of the page (the next call skips it via modules[start]); verified against the multi-page test. `moduleCount-1` underflow (0.7 OOB index / 0.8 panic) is reachable only when modules[SENTINEL]==0, i.e. an uninitialized account, where it reverts (Safe.Setup.spec:34 and my PoC).
6) execTransactionFromModuleReturnData assembly (L191-202): returnData is taken from the free pointer, 0x40 is bumped past the copied data BEFORE postModuleExecution encodes the guard call and the event, so nothing clobbers it; no external call occurs between `execute` and `returndatacopy`, so returndatasize() is the inner call's; the block satisfies the memory-safe rules for 0.8 builds; an unaligned free pointer is permitted by Solidity.
7) Module guard hooks: the guard is read before execution (L114) and the same guard gets the post hook even if the module tx replaced/removed it (test "is called when removed"); checkAfterModuleExecution receives success=false on inner failure by design. Module reentrancy into execTransaction/execTransactionFromModule nests correctly; the absence of a reentrancy guard is a documented design choice (ReentrancyTransactionGuard example).
8) GuardManager (GuardManager.sol:77-104): supportsInterface is invoked through a `view` interface (STATICCALL) before the sstore, so no reentrancy; a guard that reverts bricks execTransaction, which is documented (IGuardManager.sol:20-22, docs/overview.md:50) and recoverable via a module calling setGuard(0) (module path has no tx guard). setGuard(address(this)) fails GS300 with the shipped handlers (they do not report the ITransactionGuard id); even with a custom handler returning true, the resulting self-call has a fixed `checkTransaction` selector and cannot reach an `authorized` function. checkAfterExecution after a failed inner call (Safe.sol:226-228) is intended.
9) Storage-slot collisions: the three constants in SafeStorage.sol:61-73 equal keccak256 of their documented strings (verified), differ from ERC-1967 implementation/admin/beacon/rollback slots and from sequential slots 0-8; mapping slots are keccak of 64-byte preimages so a collision with these 26-35-byte string preimages would require a keccak collision. Layout (singleton 0, modules 1, owners 2, ownerCount 3, threshold 4, nonce 5, _deprecatedDomainSeparator 6, signedMessages 7, approvedHashes 8) matches SafeStorage.sol and the StorageAccessible "can read instantiated Safe" test; SecuredSignatureValidator (post-audit #1115) declares no state, so no shift.
10) FallbackManager (FallbackManager.sol:19-88): GS400 blocks handler==self. Independently, the 3-byte-selector attack described in the comment cannot work on 1.5.0 even without GS400: with calldatasize<4 the appended caller yields at most 19 bytes of arguments, while every `authorized` function needs >=32 bytes, so the 0.7.6 calldata-length check reverts; with calldatasize>=4 both dispatches see the same selector, so a match executes with the original (non-self) msg.sender and fails GS031 (my PoC with a bouncing handler left owners unchanged). fallback is non-payable (value+data reverts, documented at IFallbackManager.sol:18); empty calldata goes to receive(). A handler that is itself a Safe pointing back (A<->B) only recurses until OOG, a self-inflicted DoS. A handler running as EIP-7702-delegated Safe code executes with its own address as `this`, so msg.sender==this still fails. Consequently the pre-1.3.0 migration edge (a 1.1.1/1.2.0 Safe with handler==self kept by migrateSingleton) is not exploitable either.
11) StorageAccessible: getStorageAt's `length << 5` (L19) wraps only for length>=2^251, where the loop runs out of gas before returning (view, no state effect); `add(offset,index)` wrap merely reads other public slots. simulateAndRevert (L35-48) is permissionless and lets anyone run arbitrary code in the Safe's context (including self-calls that pass `authorized`), but it unconditionally reverts (L45), so no state change, value transfer, or externally observable effect survives; this is the long-standing, audited design relied on by CompatibilityFallbackHandler.simulate.
12) EIP-7702 and `authorized`: a delegated EOA sending a transaction to itself has msg.sender==address(this), bypassing signatures and guards for all `authorized` functions. Inherent to EIP-7702 (the key can re-delegate at will), so no threshold/guard can bind the EOA key; no new consequence, not reported.
13) Owner==address(this) edge cases: requireIsValidOwner (L120) gates on isThisDelegatedAccount(), which reads the account's own code via EXTCODECOPY; a regular SafeProxy never passes, a delegated EOA passes for add/remove/swap (tests pass), and a state where self is an owner but the account is not delegated cannot execute Safe code, so no stuck owner.
14) 0.8.x builds: only `--ownerCount` and `moduleCount-1` become checked (cases already unreachable or already reverting); shifts remain unchecked; no behavioral divergence in the managers.
15) Post-audit commits: #1115 (SecuredSignatureValidator) introduces no storage and does not touch the managers; #1123 is confined to CompatibilityFallbackHandler and is outside this lens.

findings.title: EIP-7702 delegation to the Safe singleton has no initialization protection: a delegated-but-unset-up EOA is claimable by anyone, and a relayer-sponsored authorization can be hijacked by a third party
findings.description: The 1.5.0 singleton is explicitly designed to be usable as an EIP-7702 delegation target (contracts/common/EIP7702.sol:15-28; contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:120 allows `owner == address(this)` only when `isThisDelegatedAccount()`; contracts/interfaces/ISafe.sol:58 says a Safe owning itself 'is a valid setup for EIP-7702 delegations'). However the only thing that gates `setup()` is `threshold == 0` (contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:49), and `threshold = 1` is written by the constructor only into the singleton's own storage (contracts/Safe.sol:99-103). An EOA that delegates to the singleton starts with `threshold == 0` in its own storage, so `setup()` (contracts/Safe.sol:108-134) is callable by any `msg.sender` with arbitrary owners; nothing in Safe/SafeL2 ties initialization to the EOA (no `msg.sender == address(this)` requirement when `isThisDelegatedAccount()`, no EOA signature over the setup parameters). `isThisDelegatedAccount()` is used nowhere else (grep: only OwnerManager.sol:120). For CREATE2 proxies this is mitigated by the factory's atomic initializer call (contracts/proxies/SafeProxyFactory.sol:66-77), but no equivalent exists for 7702. Unlike a fresh proxy, a 7702 EOA already holds ETH/tokens, so takeover is immediately profitable. The repository's only acknowledgement is a comment in a test helper (test/utils/setup.ts:122-124: 'this process is UNSAFE ... your Safe setup can be front-run by anyone'); the user-facing natspec (ISafe.sol:57-63) only warns about proxies and presents 7702 as a valid setup without mentioning this. Safe's external `safe-eip7702` proxy (commits the setup-data hash into the delegate bytecode) is the known mitigation but is not referenced anywhere in this repo.
findings.attack_path: Sponsored flow: victim EOA signs an EIP-7702 authorization tuple {chainId, Safe singleton, nonce = current EOA nonce} for a relayer to include in a type-4 tx together with `setup([victim],1,...)`. Authorization tuples are not bound to a transaction sender, so an attacker who sees the tuple (mempool, relayer API, shared bundle) submits their own type-4 tx {authorizationList:[tuple], to: victim, data: setup([attacker],1,0,'',0,0,0,0)} with higher priority fee. The delegation is applied and the attacker becomes the sole owner; the relayer's tx then fails (stale authorization nonce + GS200). The attacker drains the EOA via execTransaction with their own signature. Non-sponsored but non-atomic flow (delegate in one tx, setup in a later one) is trivially claimable in the gap. Verified on hardhat: the prior-stage PoC docs/security-review/poc/eip7702-setup-frontrun.spec.ts passes (attacker takes over and drains half the balance), and an additional test (scratchpad) confirmed the sponsored-authorization hijack: attacker reused the victim's authorization in its own tx, became owner, code at victim == 0xef0100||singleton, and the relayer's subsequent setup reverted.
findings.evidence: contracts/Safe.sol:99-103 `constructor() { threshold = 1; }` (singleton storage only); contracts/Safe.sol:117 `function setup(...) external override` with no sender/authority check; contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:49 `if (threshold > 0) revertWithError("GS200");` is the sole re-init guard; contracts/common/EIP7702.sol:15-28 `isThisDelegatedAccount()`; contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:120 only use of it; contracts/interfaces/ISafe.sol:57-63 natspec; test/utils/setup.ts:122-134 helper that models the exact unsafe flow (delegate, then setup in a separate tx) with the comment acknowledging front-running. Test run: `AUDIT_LOCAL_SOLC=1 npx hardhat test docs/security-review/poc/eip7702-setup-frontrun.spec.ts` -> passing; scratchpad test `audit: EIP-7702 sponsored authorization hijack` -> passing.
findings.recommendation: At minimum document prominently (ISafe.setup natspec, docs/overview.md, CHANGELOG 1.5.0 section) that the singleton MUST NOT be used as a direct EIP-7702 delegation target unless `setup` is executed atomically in a self-sponsored type-4 transaction, that sponsored authorizations are hijackable, and point to the safe-eip7702 proxy. Consider an in-code mitigation for delegated accounts, e.g. in `setup()`: `if (isThisDelegatedAccount() && msg.sender != address(this)) revertWithError(...)` (forces the EOA itself to initialise, which closes the sponsored-hijack path), or require an EOA signature over the setup parameters when `isThisDelegatedAccount()`.

findings.title: Regression in 1.5.0 OwnerManager: a legacy self-owner (allowed in Safe <=1.2.0) can no longer be removed or swapped after migrating a non-EIP-7702 Safe to 1.5.0 (GS203), whereas 1.3.0/1.4.1 allowed it
findings.description: PR #1062 (commit 0227664, 'Prevent Self-Ownership for Non-EIP-7702 Safes') refactored owner validation so that `removeOwner` (contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:89-99, line 93) and `swapOwner` (lines 104-112, line 106) both call `requireCanRemoveOwner` (lines 139-143), which calls `requireIsValidOwner(owner)` (lines 118-122). `requireIsValidOwner` reverts with GS203 when `owner == address(this) && !isThisDelegatedAccount()`. Before #1062 the removal check was only `owner != 0 && owner != SENTINEL` (see `git show 0227664 -- contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol`), and 1.3.0/1.4.1 likewise did not reject `address(this)` as the owner being removed. Safe 1.1.1 and 1.2.0 did not prevent a Safe from being added as its own owner. Consequently, a legacy Safe that lists itself as an owner and migrates to 1.5.0 (via `changeMasterCopy` for 1.1.1/1.2.0, or via contracts/libraries/SafeMigration.sol for any later version that inherited the config) is left with a permanently un-removable, un-swappable phantom owner: it cannot sign (it is a proxy, not a 7702 EOA), it counts toward `ownerCount`, and it can never be cleaned up. The intent of #1062 was to block *adding* a non-7702 self-owner; blocking *removal* of a pre-existing one is the opposite of what a footgun-fix should do. Not a fund-loss issue (no privilege escalation: `v==1` self-approval needs `msg.sender == Safe`, which already requires an authorised Safe tx, and CompatibilityFallbackHandler.sol:83 passes executor `address(0)`), but a concrete migration regression that the migration test-suite (test/migration/*) does not cover because it only migrates Safes with a single EOA owner.
findings.attack_path: Not attacker-driven; correctness/DoS of owner management. Reproduction (verified with a scratchpad hardhat test against the repo's shipped 1.1.1/1.2.0/1.4.1 bytecode in test/json/safeDeployment.json): (1) deploy a 1.1.1 proxy and `setup([user1, proxy], 1, ...)` -> succeeds, `isOwner(proxy) == true`; (2) upgrade to the 1.5.0 singleton via `changeMasterCopy`; (3) `removeOwner(user1, proxy, 1)` and `swapOwner(user1, proxy, user2)` executed as Safe transactions both revert with GS203; `addOwnerWithThreshold(user2,1)` still works. (4) Same legacy Safe upgraded to 1.4.1 instead: `removeOwner(user1, proxy, 1)` succeeds. 1.2.0 also accepts the self-owner at setup.
findings.evidence: contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:93 `requireCanRemoveOwner(prevOwner, owner);` in removeOwner; :106 `requireCanRemoveOwner(prevOwner, oldOwner);` in swapOwner; :139-143 `requireCanRemoveOwner` -> `requireIsValidOwner(owner)`; :118-122 `if (owner == address(0) || owner == SENTINEL_OWNERS || (owner == address(this) && !isThisDelegatedAccount())) revertWithError("GS203");`. Pre-#1062 code (git show 0227664): removeOwner had `if (owner == address(0) || owner == SENTINEL_OWNERS) revertWithError("GS203");` and swapOwner checked `address(this)` only for `newOwner`. Scratchpad test output: '1.1.1 allows the Safe to be its own owner; after upgrade to 1.5.0 the self-owner cannot be removed/swapped' PASS; '1.4.1 (for comparison) allows removing a legacy self-owner' PASS; '1.2.0 also allows self-owner (sanity)' PASS.
findings.recommendation: In `requireCanRemoveOwner`, do not apply the `address(this)` restriction to the owner being removed; keep only the null/sentinel check plus the linked-list consistency check (as pre-#1062 and as in 1.3.0/1.4.1), e.g. `if (owner == address(0) || owner == SENTINEL_OWNERS) revertWithError("GS203"); if (owners[prevOwner] != owner) revertWithError("GS205");`. Add a migration test that upgrades a <=1.2.0 Safe with a self-owner and asserts the self-owner can be removed. If the behaviour is intentionally kept, document it in the migration notes/CHANGELOG.
