findings.title: local-verify never fails the deploy pipeline: bytecode mismatch is only printed, then Sourcify/Etherscan verification proceeds
findings.description: `local-verify` is the only step in the deployment pipeline that compares on-chain code with the locally compiled artifact. It computes `verifySuccess = onChainHash === localHash ? "SUCCESS" : "FAILURE"` (src/tasks/local_verify.ts:41) and then only `console.log`s the result (line 42). It never throws, never sets `process.exitCode`, and returns normally. The composite task `deploy-contracts` (src/tasks/deploy_contracts.ts:4-7) runs `deploy` -> `local-verify` -> `sourcify` -> `etherscan-verify` sequentially with no inspection of the result, so a FAILURE line is buried in a long hardhat-deploy log while the pipeline continues to publish sources for the mismatching deployment. Note also that hardhat-deploy's deterministic path (`fetchIfDifferent`, node_modules/hardhat-deploy/dist/src/helpers.js:494-506) treats any non-empty code at the CREATE2 address as 'already deployed' and writes the deployment file without checking the code, so `local-verify` is the only code check in the flow. (README.md:65-73 even documents `local-verify` as the final step, but the code runs it before the verification uploads.)
findings.attack_path: Not attacker-triggered; operational. Example: an operator deploys on a chain whose CREATE2/factory behaviour deviates (or with a corrupted/stale local `deployments/<network>/*.json` whose `address` no longer holds the expected code). `npm run deploy-all <network>` prints `Verification status for Safe: FAILURE` once among hundreds of log lines and then successfully runs `sourcify`/`etherscan-verify`; the operator sees a green final step and submits the addresses to safe-deployments.
findings.evidence: src/tasks/local_verify.ts:41-42: `const verifySuccess = onchainBytecodeHash === localBytecodeHash ? "SUCCESS" : "FAILURE"; console.log(...)` with no throw/exit code. src/tasks/deploy_contracts.ts:4-7: `await hre.run("deploy"); await hre.run("local-verify"); await hre.run("sourcify"); await hre.run("etherscan-verify", ...)`.
findings.recommendation: Collect failures and `throw new Error(...)` (or set `process.exitCode = 1`) at the end of `local-verify` when any contract reports FAILURE, so `deploy-contracts` aborts before `sourcify`/`etherscan-verify`; optionally move `local-verify` after the uploads as the README describes, but still fail the process.

findings.title: No guard that a live deployment uses the canonical compiler settings; local-verify is self-referential so a non-canonical build still verifies as SUCCESS
findings.description: The compiler list is built from environment variables: `{ version: SOLIDITY_VERSION ?? "0.7.6", settings: soliditySettings }` where `soliditySettings = JSON.parse(SOLIDITY_SETTINGS)` (hardhat.config.ts:69, 97-102). Hardhat picks the first config whose version matches (node_modules/hardhat/internal/solidity/compilation-job.js:173-177), so a `SOLIDITY_SETTINGS` value alone (even with SOLIDITY_VERSION unset) replaces the canonical `optimizer: disabled` build. `.env.sample:15-16` explicitly tells developers to put `SOLIDITY_SETTINGS='{"viaIR":true,"optimizer":{"enabled":true,...}}'` in `.env` for coverage runs, and the same `.env` is read by `npm run deploy-all` (dotenv.config at hardhat.config.ts:40; hardhat-deploy's `deploy` task compiles first, node_modules/hardhat-deploy/dist/src/index.js:394-395). None of the deploy scripts (src/deploy/*.ts) nor the `deploy-contracts` task checks the resulting CREATE2 addresses against the CHANGELOG table or asserts `optimizer.enabled === false`. `local-verify` cannot catch this either: it re-compiles using the `settings` taken from the deployment's own metadata (src/tasks/local_verify.ts:9-27), so an optimized build at a non-canonical address verifies as SUCCESS. I confirmed the pipeline itself is sound: rebuilding the v1.5.0 commit (dc437e8) with this environment's solc 0.7.6 and salt 0 / factory 0x914d7Fec... reproduces all 13 CHANGELOG addresses exactly, so the only way to get wrong addresses is wrong sources or wrong settings, and the latter has no guard.
findings.attack_path: Operational foot-gun, not attacker-triggered: a developer runs coverage per `.env.sample` (SOLIDITY_SETTINGS set in `.env`), later runs `npm run deploy-all custom` on a new chain. Hardhat compiles an optimized/viaIR Safe, hardhat-deploy deploys it deterministically to a different CREATE2 address, `local-verify` prints SUCCESS, Etherscan verification succeeds, and a non-canonical 'Safe v1.5.0' singleton set exists on that chain and may be submitted to safe-deployments.
findings.evidence: hardhat.config.ts:69 `const soliditySettings = SOLIDITY_SETTINGS ? JSON.parse(SOLIDITY_SETTINGS) : undefined;` and :98-101 `compilers: [{ version: SOLIDITY_VERSION ?? DEFAULT_SOLIDITY_VERSION, settings: soliditySettings }, { version: DEFAULT_SOLIDITY_VERSION }]`. .env.sample:15-16 recommends optimizer/viaIR settings for coverage. src/tasks/local_verify.ts:9 `const meta = JSON.parse(deployment.metadata!)` and :27 `solcjs.compile(JSON.stringify(meta))` (settings from the deployment itself). Empirical: v1.5.0 tag rebuilt here -> Safe 0xFf51A5898e281Db6DfC7855790607438dF2ca44b, SafeL2 0xEdd160fE..., SafeMigration 0x6439e7AB... all MATCH CHANGELOG.md:29-61.
findings.recommendation: In `deploy-contracts` (or a pre-deploy check) refuse to run against a non-local network when `SOLIDITY_VERSION`/`SOLIDITY_SETTINGS` are set or when the active compiler config is not `0.7.6` with optimizer disabled; additionally compare the computed CREATE2 addresses of the artifacts with an expected-address table (as the CHANGELOG already provides) and abort on mismatch.

findings.title: Publicly-known default mnemonic is silently used as the deployer for live networks when MNEMONIC/PK are unset
findings.description: `DEFAULT_MNEMONIC = "candy maple cake sugar pudding cream honey rich smooth crumble sweet treat"` (hardhat.config.ts:58) is the well-known Truffle/Ganache phrase (account 0 = 0x627306090abaB3A6e1400e9345bC60c78a8BEf57). It is used as `sharedNetworkConfig.accounts` for every live network (mainnet, sepolia, gnosis, zksync, custom; lines 62-68, 111-134) whenever `MNEMONIC` and `PK` are both unset. The only pre-flight guard (line 54-56) checks `INFURA_KEY` for `mainnet`/`sepolia`; `gnosis`, `zksync` and `custom` have no guard at all. Because deployments are deterministic (CREATE2 through the singleton factory), the deployer key does not influence addresses, so the consequence is limited to (a) confusing 'insufficient funds' failures and (b) loss of any funds an operator sends to that address to make the deployment go through (keys for this phrase are swept by bots).
findings.attack_path: Operator runs `npm run deploy-all gnosis` without a `.env`; hardhat signs with the public key 0x6273...; the tx fails for lack of gas; the operator funds 0x6273... to retry and the funds are swept by anyone watching the well-known key. No path to a wrong singleton address.
findings.evidence: hardhat.config.ts:54 `if (["mainnet", "sepolia"].includes(argv.network) && INFURA_KEY === undefined) throw ...` (no mnemonic check, no check for gnosis/zksync/custom); :65-67 `accounts: { mnemonic: MNEMONIC ?? DEFAULT_MNEMONIC }`.
findings.recommendation: Throw when `argv.network !== "hardhat"` and neither `MNEMONIC` nor `PK` is set (or restrict `DEFAULT_MNEMONIC` to the `hardhat` network config only).

findings.title: CI workflow lacks a least-privilege `permissions:` block and pins third-party actions to mutable major tags
findings.description: `ci.yml` triggers on `[push, pull_request]` (line 2) with no top-level or job-level `permissions:` key, so `GITHUB_TOKEN` receives the repository default (potentially read/write for older repositories). All actions are referenced by major tag (`actions/checkout@v5` lines 10/21/35/53/75, `actions/setup-node@v4` line 11, `@v6` lines 23/36/54, `@v5` line 76; `actions/setup-python@v6` certora.yml:24), not by commit SHA, so a compromised or force-moved tag would execute attacker code on the runner. The setup-node versions are also inconsistent across jobs (v4/v5/v6). No `pull_request_target` is used and `ci.yml` consumes no secrets, which bounds the impact to the ephemeral runner and whatever the token can do.
findings.attack_path: Supply-chain: if an upstream action tag is retargeted, the next CI run executes it with the default-permission GITHUB_TOKEN; with a write-capable default this could push or tamper with repository content/checks. Requires compromise of the actions org or tag; no direct attacker trigger from a PR (fork PRs get a read-only token).
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:2 `on: [push, pull_request]`; no `permissions:` anywhere in ci.yml or certora.yml; ci.yml:10 `uses: actions/checkout@v5`, :11 `actions/setup-node@v4`, :23 `actions/setup-node@v6`, :76 `actions/setup-node@v5`.
findings.recommendation: Add `permissions: { contents: read }` at workflow top-level in both workflows; pin actions to full commit SHAs (with Dependabot/Renovate to bump them); unify the setup-node version.

findings.title: Certora workflow installs an unverified solc binary and unpinned-hash pip packages in a job that holds CERTORA_KEY
findings.description: The `verify` job does `wget https://github.com/ethereum/solidity/releases/download/v0.7.6/solc-static-linux` and moves it to `/usr/local/bin/solc7.6` without any checksum (certora.yml:32-34), and `pip install -r certora/requirements.txt` (line 28) with `certora-cli==7.29.2` pinned by version only (no `--require-hashes`). Both run before the step that exposes `CERTORAKEY: ${{ secrets.CERTORA_KEY }}` (line 44-45). The key is printed only as its length (`${#CERTORAKEY}`, line 42), which is fine. This job does not affect on-chain artifacts (it only feeds the Certora prover), and fork PRs do not receive the secret, so exposure is limited to a low-value prover API key via a compromised GitHub release asset or PyPI package.
findings.attack_path: Compromise of the pinned PyPI release (or GitHub release asset) -> arbitrary code on the runner -> read `CERTORAKEY` from the environment of the verify step. No path to repository write or to deployed bytecode.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/certora.yml:28 `run: pip install -r certora/requirements.txt`; :32-34 `wget .../solc-static-linux; chmod +x ...; sudo mv ...`; :45 `CERTORAKEY: ${{ secrets.CERTORA_KEY }}`; certora/requirements.txt: `certora-cli==7.29.2`.
findings.recommendation: Verify the solc download (`sha256sum --check` against the published checksum), use `pip install --require-hashes` with a hash-pinned requirements file, and add `permissions: contents: read`.

findings.title: `local-verify`/`yulcode` execute a remotely fetched solc-js build with no integrity verification (unlike Hardhat's own downloader)
findings.description: `loadSolc` calls `solc.loadRemoteVersion("v" + version, ...)` (src/utils/solc.ts:13). In the installed solc-js 0.7.6 this does a plain `https.get('https://solc-bin.ethereum.org/bin/soljson-<ver>.js')` and immediately executes the body via `requireFromString` (node_modules/solc/wrapper.js:329-339) with no keccak/list.json check and no redirect handling. Hardhat's compiler downloader, by contrast, verifies the build against `list.json` keccak256 (node_modules/hardhat/internal/solidity/compiler/downloader.js:136, 211-217). `loadSolc` runs on the operator machine during `deploy-contracts` (local-verify) where `MNEMONIC`/`PK` are in the environment. The version string comes from the deployment metadata (local_verify.ts:10), not from user input.
findings.attack_path: Requires a compromise of the solc-bin origin/CDN or an active TLS MITM against the deployer machine: the fetched JS runs in the deployer's Node process and could read `process.env.MNEMONIC`/`PK`. Hardhat's path trusts the same origin, so the incremental exposure is the missing per-file hash check.
findings.evidence: src/utils/solc.ts:13 `solc.loadRemoteVersion(`v${version}`, ...)`; node_modules/solc/wrapper.js:331 `var url = 'https://solc-bin.ethereum.org/bin/soljson-' + versionString + '.js';` and :338 `setupMethods(requireFromString(mem.toString(), ...))`.
findings.recommendation: Reuse Hardhat's verified compiler (e.g. `hre.run(TASK_COMPILE_SOLIDITY_GET_SOLC_BUILD, { solcVersion })` and load `compilerPath`) or verify the downloaded file against `list.json` keccak256 before executing it.

findings.title: Dev toolchain carries known-vulnerable transitive packages (axios 0.21.4, elliptic 6.5.4 via zksync-ethers); none reach on-chain code
findings.description: `npm audit` on the committed lockfile reports 79 advisories (4 critical, 45 high). All are devDependencies. The ones with any deploy-time footprint: `hardhat-deploy@1.0.4` (package.json:71) depends on `axios@0.21.4` (used for Etherscan API calls, node_modules/hardhat-deploy/dist/src/etherscan.js:136, 288; advisories GHSA-wf5p-g6vw-rhxx, GHSA-jr5f-v2jv-69x6) and on `zksync-ethers@5.11.0 -> ethers@5.7.2 -> @ethersproject/signing-key@5.7.0 -> elliptic@6.5.4` (GHSA-vjh7-7g9h-fjfh private-key extraction on malformed input, GHSA-977x-g7h5-7qgw). `zksync-ethers` is `require`d at module load (helpers.js:33, DeploymentFactory.js:39) but only used for `zksync: true` networks, which this config never sets (hardhat.config.ts:123-126), and transaction signing for deployments goes through Hardhat's local-accounts provider (noble secp256k1), not elliptic 6.5.4. `@openzeppelin/contracts@3.4.2` (package.json:60) is imported only by contracts/test/{ERC20Token,ERC721Token,ERC1155Token,TestImports}.sol; no production contract imports from node_modules. The lockfile itself is clean: lockfileVersion 3, every package resolved from registry.npmjs.org with an integrity hash, and CI uses `npm ci`.
findings.attack_path: No path to deployed bytecode. Realistic exposure is limited to the developer/CI machine (DoS/ReDoS in lint/test tooling, SSRF-class issues in axios only reachable with attacker-controlled URLs, which the etherscan task does not accept).
findings.evidence: package-lock.json: `node_modules/axios` 0.21.4, `node_modules/zksync-ethers/node_modules/elliptic` 6.5.4, `node_modules/elliptic` 6.6.1; `npm audit --json` metadata `{"critical":4,"high":45,"moderate":13,"low":17}`; direct packages flagged: hardhat, hardhat-deploy, @nomicfoundation/hardhat-toolbox, @openzeppelin/contracts, typescript-eslint, solc (via tmp).
findings.recommendation: Bump `hardhat-deploy` when a release drops axios 0.21.x / zksync-ethers 5.x (or add an `overrides` entry for `elliptic` and `axios`), keep `@openzeppelin/contracts` dev-only, and run `npm audit` in CI with an allow-list so new deploy-path advisories are noticed.

findings.title: Fork-only compiler escape hatch bypasses Hardhat's compiler integrity check and hard-codes the solc long version
findings.description: Commit 75e7ea7 (not upstream; part of the audit scaffolding in this fork) registers a `TASK_COMPILE_SOLIDITY_GET_SOLC_BUILD` subtask that, when `AUDIT_LOCAL_SOLC=1`, returns `require.resolve("solc/soljson.js")` with a hard-coded `longVersion: "0.7.6+commit.7338295f"` (hardhat.config.ts:19-27). This skips Hardhat's keccak256 verification of compiler builds and trusts the npm `solc` package instead (lockfile-pinned `solc@=0.7.6` with integrity). The untracked `.env` in this checkout enables it. I verified empirically that this compiler is byte-identical in output to the official build for this code base: compiling the v1.5.0 commit with it reproduces all 13 CHANGELOG 1.5.0 CREATE2 addresses. It is therefore safe for this audit environment, but it should not be merged upstream or used for a production `deploy-all`, since `longVersion` is asserted rather than derived and any future drift of the npm `solc` pin would be silently mislabelled in build-info/metadata.
findings.attack_path: None in this environment (verified equivalence). If carried into a deployment environment with `AUDIT_LOCAL_SOLC=1` and a different npm `solc` version installed, build-info/deployment metadata would claim 0.7.6+commit.7338295f while bytecode came from another compiler, defeating later source verification.
findings.evidence: hardhat.config.ts:19-29 (subtask returning `compilerPath: require.resolve("solc/soljson.js"), isSolcJs: true, version: "0.7.6", longVersion: "0.7.6+commit.7338295f"`); `.env` (untracked) contains `AUDIT_LOCAL_SOLC=1`; rebuild of dc437e8 with this compiler -> Safe 0xFf51A5898e..., MultiSend 0x2185432880..., all MATCH CHANGELOG.md:29-61.
findings.recommendation: Keep this out of upstream; if retained locally, derive `longVersion` from `require("solc").version()` and assert it equals `0.7.6+commit.7338295f`, and refuse `AUDIT_LOCAL_SOLC` when `--network` is not `hardhat`.

result.reviewed: Read end to end: package.json; package-lock.json (spot-checked programmatically: lockfileVersion 3, 0 packages without integrity, 0 packages resolved outside registry.npmjs.org; versions of hardhat 2.27.0, hardhat-deploy 1.0.4, @safe-global/safe-singleton-factory 2.0.0, solc 0.7.6, @openzeppelin/contracts 3.4.2, ethers 6.15.0, axios 0.21.4, elliptic 6.6.1 + nested 6.5.4, ws, undici, form-data etc.); hardhat.config.ts (including the two fork-only commits 75e7ea7/d1bf5f4 on top of upstream f8fc2f2, diffed against f8fc2f2 and against the v1.5.0 commit dc437e8); .github/workflows/ci.yml; .github/workflows/certora.yml; .github/CODEOWNERS; .husky/pre-commit; src/deploy/{deploy_accessors,deploy_factories,deploy_handlers,deploy_libraries,deploy_migrations,deploy_safe_l2,deploy_safe_singleton}.ts; src/tasks/{deploy_contracts,local_verify,show_codesize}.ts; src/utils/{constants,execution,multisend,proxies,solc}.ts; src/index.ts; .env.sample; the untracked local .env (contains only AUDIT_LOCAL_SOLC=1); .gitignore; .gitattributes; .nvmrc; .solhint.json; .solcover.js; .prettierrc; eslint.config.mjs; tsconfig.prod.json; certora/Makefile; certora/requirements.txt; README.md; CHANGELOG.md (compiler-settings and expected-address sections). Followed into dependencies: hardhat-deploy helpers.js (ensureCreate2DeployerReady, _deploy create2 salt handling, fetchIfDifferent, _deployOne), DeploymentsManager.js (getDeterminisityDeploymentInfo passes chainId; defaults), index.js (deploy task compiles unless --noCompile), etherscan.js (api key only in request URL/body, masked in debug output); hardhat compilation-job.js (compiler selection = first config with max satisfying version) and compiler/downloader.js (keccak verification); solc 0.7.6 wrapper.js loadRemoteVersion; @safe-global/safe-singleton-factory dist/index.js and artifacts for chains 1/100/324/11155111/31337. Empirical checks: `npm audit --json` (79 advisories, all devDependencies); `git grep` for 64-hex private keys / mnemonic / secret strings across tracked files (only the documented DEFAULT_MNEMONIC and test constants); verified .env is gitignored and untracked; computed CREATE2 addresses of the current HEAD build (they differ from CHANGELOG, e.g. Safe 0x0D0C6885...); fetched the v1.5.0 release commit dc437e8, confirmed every contract file (including comment-only NatSpec edits to MultiSend.sol) changed after the tag, rebuilt dc437e8 in a scratch worktree with the local solc 0.7.6 and confirmed all 13 CHANGELOG 1.5.0 addresses (Safe, SafeL2, SafeProxyFactory, three handlers, CreateCall, MultiSend, MultiSendCallOnly, SignMessageLib, SafeToL2Setup, SimulateTxAccessor, SafeMigration with constructor args) are reproduced exactly with factory 0x914d7Fec6aaC8cd542e72Bca78B30650d45643d7 and salt 0x00..00; worktree removed afterwards.
result.ruled_out: 1) 'Deployed addresses differ from CHANGELOG because of compiler/settings drift' — RULED OUT: the HEAD build's addresses differ only because every contract source changed after the v1.5.0 tag (NatSpec rewrites alter the metadata hash; e.g. contracts/libraries/MultiSend.sol has no imports and still differs by comments). Rebuilding the exact v1.5.0 commit with this toolchain reproduces all 13 CHANGELOG addresses byte-for-byte, so the default config (0.7.6, optimizer disabled, evm istanbul, hardhat-deploy zero salt, singleton factory from the npm package) is the canonical one. README.md:7-8 and :49-52 already warn that main is unreleased. 2) 'Wrong salt / wrong factory / constructor-arg mix-up in src/deploy' — RULED OUT: all deploy scripts use `deterministicDeployment: true` (zero salt per hardhat-deploy helpers.js:347-349) and `args: []`, except SafeMigration whose args [Safe, SafeL2, CompatibilityFallbackHandler] are read from deployment files that hardhat-deploy has just (re)written with the CREATE2-computed addresses (fetchIfDifferent/_deployOne, helpers.js:494-575), and `deploy.dependencies = ["singleton","l2","handlers"]` guarantees ordering; the SafeMigration address reproduces the CHANGELOG value. `deterministicDeployment(network)` receives the chainId string (DeploymentsManager.js:367-370), so `parseInt` is correct, and unknown chains throw (hardhat.config.ts:73-77) rather than silently falling back to the Arachnid proxy (0x4e59b4...) default. 3) 'ensureCreate2DeployerReady could fund/broadcast the factory presigned tx on the wrong chain' — RULED OUT in practice: the package only lists chains where the factory is already deployed (code != 0x), so helpers.js:258-297 is a no-op; if it did run, it uses the package's own signerAddress/funding/presigned tx, not operator-controlled values. 4) 'local-verify only compiles, does not verify bytecode' — RULED OUT: it recompiles from the stored metadata, zeroes immutable references in on-chain code and compares keccak256 of deployedBytecode (local_verify.ts:27-40); the real defects are that it is non-fatal and self-referential (reported). 5) 'pull_request_target / secrets exposure in ci.yml' — RULED OUT: ci.yml uses `pull_request`, consumes no secrets, no `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolation in `run:` steps (no script injection surface). certora.yml uses `pull_request` (fork PRs get no secrets) and prints only `${#CERTORAKEY}` (length). 6) 'Committed secrets / .env hygiene' — RULED OUT: `.env` is in .gitignore (.gitignore:11) and untracked; grep of tracked files finds no private keys or mnemonics other than the documented Truffle default and test constants (0x4242..., storage-slot hashes). 7) 'npm scripts with hidden network side effects' — only the expected ones: `build`/`prepack`/`prepublish` run `hardhat compile` (compiler download with Hardhat keccak verification), `deploy-contracts` calls Sourcify/Etherscan, `prepare: husky` only sets core.hooksPath; no postinstall, no curl|sh. 8) 'Default mnemonic could produce wrong singleton addresses' — RULED OUT: deployer identity does not enter CREATE2 addresses; only the funds-loss/confusion aspect remains (reported as informational). 9) 'hardhat.config.ts duplicate 0.7.6 compiler entries cause nondeterminism' — Hardhat deterministically picks the first entry with the max satisfying version (compilation-job.js:173-177); consequence is only that SOLIDITY_SETTINGS overrides the canonical build (reported). 10) '@openzeppelin/contracts ^3.4.2 advisories affect production' — RULED OUT: imported only by contracts/test/{ERC20Token,ERC721Token,ERC1155Token,TestImports}.sol; no non-test contract imports from node_modules. 11) 'elliptic 6.5.4 / axios 0.21.4 reach the deployment signing path' — RULED OUT: elliptic 6.5.4 sits under zksync-ethers (only used with `zksync: true` networks, never configured); deployment signing goes through Hardhat's local-accounts provider; axios is used only for Etherscan API GET/POST with config-derived URLs (etherscan.js:136, 252, 288), and the API key is masked in debug output (etherscan.js:309). 12) 'certora/Makefile `clean: git clean -fdX` deletes the operator's .env' — RULED OUT: git clean without pathspec is scoped to the cwd (certora/), so it only removes ignored files under certora/. 13) '.husky/pre-commit bypass' — the hook reads a shell variable `$allowonlytests` (line 7) while the message tells users to set `git config hooks.allowonlytests true` (line 15), so the documented bypass does not work; this fails safe (the check stays on) and is not security-relevant. 14) 'package.json `files` ships `build/` artifacts' — build/ is regenerated by `prepublish`/`prepack` on the publisher's machine; consumers should rely on safe-deployments, not on these artifacts; no concrete attack path beyond general npm-publisher trust, so not reported. 15) 'CODEOWNERS' — single catch-all rule `* @safe-global/safe-protocol`; adequate, branch-protection settings are not visible from the repo. 16) hardhat 2.27.0 / toolbox 6.1.0 / solc =0.7.6 pins — current enough; the `npm audit` entries for `hardhat`/`hardhat-toolbox` are transitive (mocha/undici/adm-zip/sentry) and dev-only.

findings.title: Post-audit functional changes beyond #1115/#1123 are absent from the 1.5.0 audit reports, the CHANGELOG 'Current version' section and docs/signatures.md
findings.description: The content diff between the Ackee-audited tree (5d26505, 2025-05-27) and HEAD (`git diff 5d26505 HEAD -- contracts/`) contains, besides #1115 and #1123, several functional changes: (1) EIP-7951 secp256r1 signer type `v == 2` in contracts/Safe.sol:354-396 plus new contracts/common/EIP7951.sol and new error codes GS027/GS028 (commit 0e91d99, 2026-01-14); (2) EIP-7702 self-ownership via `isThisDelegatedAccount()` in contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol:118-121 and new contracts/common/EIP7702.sol (commits 034184d 2025-07-10, 0227664 2025-12-12); (3) `SafeProxyFactory.proxyCreationCodehash` (contracts/proxies/SafeProxyFactory.sol:42-44, commit 1036b92); (4) assembly `domainSeparator` (contracts/Safe.sol:456-474, dd2454f); (5) storage-slot constants moved to contracts/libraries/SafeStorage.sol (6a71753). Keyword search of docs/Safe_Audit_Report_1_5_0_Certora.pdf and docs/Safe_Audit_Report_1_5_0_Ackee.pdf finds zero hits for 7951/7212/secp256r1/p256, and Ackee states 'The reviewed version of Safe is incompatible with EIP-7702 smart accounts', so these changes post-date both audits. CHANGELOG.md lines 8-16 ('Current version') list only the #1115 change; the whole CHANGELOG has no mention of secp256r1/EIP-7951/EIP-7702/proxyCreationCodehash, and docs/signatures.md (read in full) documents only signature types 0, 1, 27-30 and >30 — the `v == 2` secp256r1 encoding (`r` = owner address, `s` = pointer to 128 bytes `r||s||qx||qy`, GS027/GS028) is undocumented there. The task brief's premise that only #1115 and #1123 landed after the audits is therefore not supported by the repository evidence. I could not determine (public RPCs are blocked by the proxy, no safe-deployments package installed) whether the deployed 1.5.0 singleton (0xFf51A5898e281Db6DfC7855790607438dF2ca44b) was built with or without these changes; `VERSION` is still "1.5.0" at contracts/Safe.sol:58.

findings.title: #1115 strict return-data semantics are not covered by tests (only the revert case is); PoC confirms documented behaviour
findings.description: The only tests added by #1115 are the two 'isValidSignature reverts' cases (test/core/Safe.Signatures.spec.ts:1102-1144 and test/handlers/CompatibilityFallbackHandler.spec.ts:232-281). None of the behaviours the CHANGELOG calls a breaking change (CHANGELOG.md:16: exactly 32 bytes, magic in first 4 bytes, remaining 28 bytes zero) is exercised: no test for 33-byte or 64-byte (trailing) returns, 31/4/0-byte (short) returns, dirty low bits, magic right-aligned, or an EOA/codeless address used as a `v == 0` signer. A repo-wide grep for mock validators returning crafted data (`givenMethodReturn|givenCalldataReturn|1626ba7e`) finds only full-magic returns. I wrote and ran a PoC spec (docs/security-review/poc/post-audit-erc1271-strict-return.spec.ts, 12 passing, left uncommitted) which confirms, under solc 0.7.6, that contracts/common/SecuredSignatureValidator.sol:23 accepts exactly `0x1626ba7e || 28 zero bytes` and rejects (GS024) 33/64/31/4/0-byte returns, dirty low bits and right-aligned magic; it also confirms with a legacy high-level caller compiled by the same solc that the pre-#1115 code accepted the 33-byte, 64-byte and dirty-low-bit cases, exactly as the CHANGELOG states. So the implementation is correct and the CHANGELOG is accurate, but a future refactor (e.g. relaxing `result.length == 32` to `>= 32`, or switching to ABI decoding) would not be caught by the suite.
findings.attack_path: None directly; regression risk only. A future change that re-enables lenient decoding would silently widen what counts as a valid contract signature without any test failing.
findings.evidence: Safe.Signatures.spec.ts:1102-1144 and CompatibilityFallbackHandler.spec.ts:232-281 use only `revertingSignatureValidatorContract` (test/utils/contracts.ts:86-95, `revert("isValidSignature reverted")`). PoC run output: 'checkNSignatures: 33 bytes (one trailing byte) => GS024; legacy high-level call => true', '32 bytes, dirty low bits => GS024; legacy high-level call => true', '31 bytes (short) => GS024; legacy high-level call => revert', 'exactly 32 bytes, magic left-aligned => valid; legacy => true'.
findings.recommendation: Port the PoC cases into test/core/Safe.Signatures.spec.ts (and the CompatibilityFallbackHandler suite): 32-byte success, 33/64-byte trailing data, 31/4/0-byte short data, dirty low bits, right-aligned magic, codeless address as v==0 signer, all expecting GS024 except the exact-32 case.

findings.title: Error-code documentation is stale/ambiguous after post-audit changes: GS024 now covers reverts, codeless signers and bad return sizes; GS027 is reused with a different meaning than in 1.3.0
findings.description: (a) docs/error_codes.md:41-43 describes GS024 as 'The contract signer returned an invalid value (not EIP1271_MAGIC_VALUE)'. After #1115 (contracts/Safe.sol:295 + contracts/common/SecuredSignatureValidator.sol:22-23) GS024 is also raised when `isValidSignature` reverts (including out-of-gas in the callee), when the signer address has no code (the low-level `staticcall` has no EXTCODESIZE check, so an EOA returns success with empty data — confirmed by PoC), and when the return data is not exactly 32 bytes. The debugging hint ('check that the contract signer ... returns the correct value') therefore misses the most common new cause (inner revert, e.g. a nested Safe's GS025/GS026 now surfaces as GS024, as test/core/Safe.Signatures.spec.ts:514-516 notes). (b) GS027 was defined in the 1.3.0 changelog (CHANGELOG.md:300) as 'dataHash must equal hash of data' for contract signatures; the post-audit EIP-7951 commit reuses GS027 at contracts/Safe.sol:368 for 'Invalid secp256r1 signature location' (docs/error_codes.md:50) without noting the reuse. Tooling or docs that map error codes across versions will mislabel one of the two.
findings.attack_path: None; developer/integrator confusion only (misdiagnosed signature failures, wrong error labels in cross-version tooling).
findings.evidence: docs/error_codes.md:41-43 (GS024 text); contracts/common/SecuredSignatureValidator.sol:22-23 (`owner.staticcall(data)`; `success && result.length == 32 && ...`); CHANGELOG.md:300 ('revert with a `GS027` error code' for data-hash mismatch, 1.3.0 section) vs contracts/Safe.sol:368 and docs/error_codes.md:50 (secp256r1 location). PoC: 'EOA used as a v=0 contract signer => GS024'.
findings.recommendation: Update the GS024 entry to list all triggers (revert/OOG in signer, no code at signer address, return data length != 32, value != magic) and the nested-Safe mapping; add a note to the GS027 entry (and the CHANGELOG 'Current version' section) that the code was previously used in 1.3.0 for the removed data-hash check.

result.ruled_out: 1) Byte layout of the magic check (SecuredSignatureValidator.sol:23): `bytes32(EIP1271_MAGIC_VALUE)` is a bytes4->bytes32 widening, i.e. left-aligned 0x1626ba7e||28 zero bytes; a Solidity `bytes4` return is ABI-encoded identically (left-aligned, cleaned). PoC confirms a validator returning exactly that word passes, and that a nested Safe+CompatibilityFallbackHandler owner returns exactly 32 bytes (`ethers.provider.call` raw result == 0x1626ba7e00…00), so older Safes (>=1.3.0, which expose isValidSignature(bytes32,bytes)) remain valid owners. Pre-1.3.0 Safes (only isValidSignature(bytes,bytes), selector 0x20c13b0b) never worked with the 1.3.0+ core and are not a #1115 regression. 2) Breaking change scope: PoC with a legacy high-level caller compiled by the same solc 0.7.6 (legacy ABI coder) shows the old path accepted 33/64-byte trailing data and dirty low bits (decoder cleans via shr/shl, only checks returndatasize >= 32) and rejected short/right-aligned data; the new path rejects all but exact 32 bytes. This matches CHANGELOG.md:16 exactly; only hand-written-assembly validators are affected. Documented, accepted -> not a finding. 3) Swallowed reverts creating a new state-affecting outcome: `validateContractSignature` returning false always leads to `revertWithError("GS024")` at Safe.sol:295, so checkNSignatures/checkSignatures/execTransaction still revert as a whole; PoC shows execTransaction with a bad contract signer reverts with GS024 and `nonce` is unchanged — no nonce burn, no griefing beyond what was already possible. The only observable change is revert data (nested Safe GS025/GS026 -> GS024), which is intentional (test comment Safe.Signatures.spec.ts:514-516). 4) OOG / 63-64 forwarding: a gas-burning validator makes the inner staticcall fail; the outer still has the 1/64 reserve and reverts with GS024 (PoC, 3M gas limit). Previously it bubbled an empty revert. Both revert; attacker pays. 5) Returndata bomb via the new full-returndata copy in `(bool, bytes memory) = owner.staticcall(...)`: the callee must itself pay quadratic memory expansion to produce the data, so the outer's copy at most doubles cost; a plain gas-burner already consumes all forwarded gas in both old and new code; no new vector. 6) `abi.decode(result,(bytes32))` is guarded by short-circuit `result.length == 32`, and decoding a 32-byte static word cannot revert in 0.7.6 (legacy) or 0.8.x (coder v2, bytes32 needs no validation). 7) staticcall vs. previous high-level call: `isValidSignature` is `view`, so 0.7.6 already emitted STATICCALL; no change in static context, reentrancy surface, or gas forwarding (both forward gas()). The 0x-exploit test ('should revert if EIP-1271 check changes state') still passes. 8) Removal of the implicit EXTCODESIZE check: a codeless/EOA address as v==0 signer now yields GS024 instead of an empty revert (PoC). Precompiles as signer targets were considered: none (0x01-0x0a, 0x0b-0x11 BLS, 0x100 p256verify) can return exactly the 32-byte left-aligned magic for attacker-chosen input without a hash preimage, and the owner-membership check (Safe.sol:405) still follows. 9) Memory safety of the signature pointer: `contractSignature` points inside `signatures` (Safe.sol:291); abi.encodeWithSelector reads `mload(contractSignature)` bytes which were bounds-checked at Safe.sol:272/282 with SafeMath — identical to the pre-#1115 encoding. 10) Storage layout / ABI: SecuredSignatureValidator has no state variables; `validateContractSignature` is internal; Safe's external ABI is unchanged; inheritance linearization (ISignatureValidatorConstants now via SecuredSignatureValidator) compiles and constants are unchanged. 11) SafeL2 behaviour: checkNSignatures is view and emits nothing; SafeL2's SafeMultiSigTransaction/SafeModuleTransaction events are emitted in onBefore* hooks unaffected by #1115. 12) EIP-170: artifacts built from HEAD sources with solc 0.7.6 / optimizer off give Safe 20869 B and SafeL2 21649 B runtime, both under 24576 B. 13) #1123 correctness: returndata of Safe.simulateAndRevert is [success][len][data] (StorageAccessible.sol:42-45); simulate copies the first 64 bytes to scratch, allocates `responseEncodedSize = mload(0x20)+0x20`, copies `[len][data]` to `response`, so `mload(response) == mload(0x20) == len` and `revert(add(response,0x20), mload(response))` returns exactly `len` bytes; the new byte-exact test (CompatibilityFallbackHandler.spec.ts:352-369) passes. Over-long `len` from a non-Safe caller makes returndatacopy revert (all gas) as the comment at 163-168 states; the `badSimulator` modes test covers malformed callers; a wrapping `add(mload(0x20),0x20)` only harms a malicious caller that is not a Safe (documented 'only for Safes'). 14) Same bug pattern elsewhere: every other revert/return site uses `returndatasize()` consistently with its copy (Safe.sol:212-213, SafeProxy.sol:72-76, SafeProxyFactory.sol:72-73, MultiSend*.sol, FallbackManager.sol:80-84, StorageAccessible.sol:43-45 = size+0x40 matching [success][size][data]); ErrorMessage.sol:29 reverts 0x64 = 4+32+32+32 for a 5-byte string; SimulateTxAccessor.sol:61-65 and ModuleManager.sol:197-201 size allocation and length word consistently. No other instance found. 15) Other code-level post-audit changes examined and found behaviour-preserving: SafeMath.sub (`return a - b` after `require(b <= a)`), storage-slot constants moved to file-level in SafeStorage.sol with unchanged hashes (0x6c9a…18d5, 0x4a20…34c8, 0xb104…9947), Enum/ErrorMessage file moves, domainSeparator assembly (same keccak256(abi.encode(typehash, chainid, address)) layout, 96 bytes), SafeToL2Migration deletion (documented in 1.5.0 CHANGELOG). EIP-7951 (Safe.sol:354-396, EIP7951.sol) and EIP-7702 self-ownership (OwnerManager.sol:114-144, EIP7702.sol) were only scoped for audit-coverage/doc consistency here (finding 1); their logic is out of this lens and left to the signature/ownership lenses. 16) CHANGELOG/doc consistency for #1115 itself: CHANGELOG.md:12-16 and ISignatureValidator.sol:27-28 accurately describe the new semantics; only docs/error_codes.md GS024 text is stale (finding 3). 17) Review-scaffolding commits 75e7ea7/d1bf5f4 touch only hardhat.config.ts (inert unless AUDIT_LOCAL_SOLC=1) and docs/security-review/poc specs — no production impact.
